Each puzzle instance has a task id and a test input grid. Tasks recur across the
stream with fresh inputs. Each instance is a separate conversation: the next one
starts without this one's messages.

On every message you must choose exactly one action and put it as a JSON object
on the last line of your reply:
  {"action": "submit", "grid": [[0, 1, 2], [3, 4, 5]]}   submit an output grid
  {"action": "request_demos"}                            ask for one more demonstration pair for this task
  {"action": "finish"}                                   end the instance, once it is over
Grids are lists of rows; cells are integers 0-9; dimensions are 1-30.

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

Scoring: an instance you solve costs 1 for each wrong submission and 1 for
each demo request. An instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt
cap is reached, and one that ends unsolved costs the whole budget, 16, however
many submissions and demo requests it used. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

import os,glob,re,json
def load():
    d=os.path.normpath(os.environ['RLM_SESSION_DIR'])
    t=open(d+'/../../sessions/'+os.path.basename(d)+'.jsonl').read().replace('\\n','\n'); G={}
    for m in re.finditer(r'(Demo pair \d+ (?:input|output)|Test input) \((\d+)x(\d+)\):\n',t):
        k,h,w=m[1],int(m[2]),int(m[3])
        rows=[r.split() for r in t[m.end():].split('\n')[:h]]
        if k not in G and all(len(r)==w and all(x.isdigit() for x in r) for r in rows):
            G[k]=[[int(x) for x in r] for r in rows]
    return G
G=load(); print(sorted(G))
inp=G['Demo pair 1 input']; out=G['Demo pair 1 output']
# find nonzero cells in input
cells=[(i,j,v) for i,r in enumerate(inp) for j,v in enumerate(r) if v!=1]
print(cells)

def solve(g):
    h,w=len(g),len(g[0]); bg=g[0][0]
    # find object cells
    cells=[(i,j,g[i][j]) for i in range(h) for j in range(w) if g[i][j]!=bg]

        while 0<=nx+dr<h and 0<=ny+dc<w and g[nx][ny]==bg:
            out[nx+dr][ny+dc]=v; nx+=dr; ny+=dc

from collections import defaultdict
def f(g):
    h,w=len(g),len(g[0]); bg=g[0][0]
    O=[row[:] for row in g]
    from collections import defaultdict
    lines={}  # line id -> list of (r,c,v)
    for r in range(h):
        for c in range(w):
            v=g[r][c]
            if v!=bg:
                md=r-c; ad=r+c
                lines.setdefault(md,[]).append((v,r,c))
                lines.setdefault(ad,[]).append((v,r,c))
    for key,pts in lines.items():
        if len(pts)<2: continue
        # pick the two cells whose colors differ or are furthest apart along the line
        pts.sort(key=lambda p:p[1])
        a,b=pts[0],pts[-1]
        dr=(b[0]-a[0]); dc=(b[1]-a[1])
        step=abs(dr) or abs(dc)
        sgn=1 if dr>0 else -1 if dc>0 else 1
        x,y=a[1],a[2]
        while True:
            x+=sgn*step*(dr and abs(dr)!=0)
        break
    return O

def f(g):
    H,W=len(g),len(g[0])
    vals=dict(Counter(x for r in g for x in r))
    bg=max(vals,key=lambda v:vals[v])
    o={v:[(i,j) for i,row in enumerate(g) for j,x in enumerate(row) if x==v] for v in set(vals)-{bg}}
    out=[row[:] for row in g]
    def fill(v,p,step):
        r,c=p; dr,dc=step
        while 0<=r+dr<H and 0<=c+dc<W and out[r+dr][c+dc]==bg:
            out[r+dr][c+dc]=v; r+=dr; c+=dc
    for v,cells in o.items():
        D=defaultdict(list)
        for r,c in cells: D[r-c].append((r,c)); D[r+c].append((r,c))
        for key,line in D.items():
            line.sort()
            if len(line)<2: continue
            # directional runs on this diagonal: consecutive unit steps along (±1,±1)
            used=set(); runs=[]
            for p in sorted(line):
                if p in used: continue
                start=p; q=None
                while True:
                    hits=[o2 for o2 in line if (abs(o2[0]-q[0])==1 and abs(o2[1]-q[1])==1)]
                    if not hits: break
                    q=hits[0]; used.add(q)
                chain=list(map(sorted,sorted({p,q}))) if False else None
                # build full contiguous chain from start forward
                cur=start
                path=[cur]
                while True:
                    nxt=[o2 for o2 in line if o2!=cur and abs(o2[0]-cur[0])==1 and abs(o2[1]-cur[1])==1]
                    if not nxt: break
                    n=min(nxt,key=lambda p2:abs(p2[0]-cur[0])+abs(p2[1]-cur[1]))
                    step=(n[0]-cur[0],n[1]-cur[1])
                    path.append(n)
                    cur=n
                runs.append(path)
                used|=set(path)
            for path in runs:
                for e,sgn in [(-1*path[0][0],None)]: pass
                # compute extension distance from each end, pick minimal
                best=None
                for e in [path[0],path[-1]]:
                    d=e
                    # direction away from chain
                    step=None
                    if e==path[0]: step=(-(path[1][0]-path[0][0]), -(path[1][1]-path[0][1]))
                    else: step=(path[-1][0]-path[-2][0], path[-1][1]-path[-2][1])
                    dist = sum(abs(step[i]) for i in range(2)) - 1
                    # distance to nearest edge along this diagonal step
                    steps_needed=H if False else 0
                    rr,cc=e[0]+step[0],e[1]+step[1]
                    while 0<=rr<H and 0<=cc<W:
                        steps_needed+=1
                        if not (0<=rr+step[0]<H and 0<=cc+step[1]<W): break
                        rr+=step[0]; cc+=step[1]
                    # distance to boundary along this diagonal
                    if steps_needed==0: continue
                    cand=(min(steps_needed, max(H-e[0]-abs(step[0]), W-e[1]-abs(step[1]))) , steps_needed, (steps_needed==1,step,e)) if False else None
                    if best is None or cand[1]<best[1]: best=cand
                if best is not None:
                    pass
                return out
    return out

def solve(g):
    H,W=len(g),len(g[0])
    cnt=Counter(x for r in g for x in r)
    bg=max(cnt,key=lambda v:cnt[v])
    cells={(r,c):g[r][c] for r in range(H) for c in range(W) if g[r][c]!=bg}
    out=[row[:] for row in g]
    seen=set()
    for k in set(r-c for r,c in cells) | set(r+c for r,c in cells):
        if k in set(r-c for r,c in cells):
            pos=lambda rr,cc: rr-c
            step=1
        else:
            pos=lambda rr,cc: rr+cc; step=-1
        pts=sorted([(rr,cc,cells[(rr,cc)]) for rr,cc in cells if pos(rr,cc)==k], key=lambda t:t[:2])
        if len(pts)<2: continue
        # split into runs of consecutive diagonal positions (along the diagonal)
        runs=[]; cur=[pts[0]]
        for pt in pts[1:]:
            pr,pcc,pv=cur[-1]; r,c,v=pt
            dr,dc=r-pr,c-pcc
            if abs(dr)==abs(dc): cur.append(pt)
            else: runs.append(cur); cur=[pt]
        runs.append(cur)
        for run in runs:
            if len(run)<2: continue
            r,c,v=run[0]
            while True:
                r-=step*(1 if False else 0)
            # simpler: step along diagonal direction
                rr,cc=r-1,c-1
                while 0<=rr<H and 0<=cc<W and cells.get((rr,cc),bg)==bg:
                    out[rr][cc]=v; rr-=1; cc-=1
                rr,cc=r+1,c+1
                while 0<=rr<H and 0<=cc<W and cells.get((rr,cc),bg)==bg:

    out=[r[:] for r in g]
    seen=set()

            c2=g[r][c]; dx,dy=(-1,-1)

                if 0<=rr<H and 0<=cc<W and g[rr][cc]==c2:
                    a,b=minmax(rr-r,cc-c); b2=a*min(abs(a),abs(b))-b*a

                    # fill along the line both sides from the pair ends

import math
from collections import Counter
def solve(g):
    H,W=len(g),len(g[0])
    bg=Counter(x for r in g for x in r).most_common(1)[0][0]
    out=[r[:] for r in g]; seen=set()
    # pairs with a cell's two diagonal neighbors same color (diagonal pair) -> extend from each end of the pair both directions along line, plus fill the perpendicular row/col segment
    for dr,dc in [(1,1),(1,-1)]:
        for r in range(H):
            for c in range(W):
                if g[r][c]!=bg: continue
                rr,cc=r+dr,c+dc
                if 0<=rr<H and 0<=cc<W and g[rr][cc]==g[r][c]:
                    seen.add((r,c)); seen.add((rr,cc))
                    step=(dr,dc); sgn=1
                    while True:
                        cr,cs=r-dr*sgn,c-dc*sgn
                        cr-=dr; cs-=dc
                        if not(0<=cr<H and 0<=cs<W) or g[cr][cs]!=bg: break
                        out[cr][cs]=g[r][c]
                    cr,cs=rr+dr*sgn,cc+dc*sgn
                    while True:
                        cr+=dr; cs+=dc
                        if not(0<=cr<H and 0<=cs<W) or g[cr][cs]!=bg: break
                        out[cr][cs]=g[r][c]
                    # perpendicular fill between the two cells
                    c2=g[r][c]
                    cc_=(r+rr)//2; rs_=(c+cc)//2
                    # horizontal line through pair
                    hrow=c
                    for k2 in range(rs_,rr+1): 
                        kr=(k2+r)/2
                        k2=int(k2)
                    # simple version: fill row r? no—demo8 fills diagonals only. Just do the two-diag fills.
    return out

from collections import defaultdict
def load():
    d=os.path.normpath(os.environ['RLM_SESSION_DIR'])
    t=open(d+'/../../sessions/'+os.path.basename(d)+'.jsonl').read().replace('\\n','\n'); G={}
    for m in re.finditer(r'(Demo pair \d+ (?:input|output)|Test input) \((\d+)x(\d+)\):\n',t):
        k,h,w=m[1],int(m[2]),int(m[3])
        rows=[r.split() for r in t[m.end():].split('\n')[:h]]
        if k not in G and all(len(r)==w and all(x.isdigit() for x in r) for r in rows):
            G[k]=[[int(x) for x in r] for r in rows]
    return G
G=load()
def f(gi):
    H,W=len(gi),len(gi[0]);bg=gi[0][0];out=[row[:] for row in gi]
    cells=defaultdict(list)
    for r in range(H):
        for c in range(W):
            if gi[r][c]!=bg: cells[gi[r][c]].append((r,c))
    shapes=[]
    for v,ps in cells.items():
        pts=set(ps)
        if len(pts)<2: continue
        shapes.append((v,pts))
    if not shapes: return out
    # centroids of multi-point shapes
    info=[]
    for v,pts in shapes:
        rs=[p[0] for p in pts];cs=[p[1] for p in pts]
        sc=((max(rs)+min(rs))/2,(max(cs)+min(cs))/2)
        a=min(pts); b=max(pts,key=lambda p:(p[0],p[1]))
        dr=b[0]-a[0]; dc=b[1]-a[1]
        g=math.gcd(abs(dr),abs(dc))
        s=(dr//g,dc//g)
        info.append((v,a,b,s,sc,sorted(pts)))
    for idx,v,beg,endpt,s,sc,ps in info:
        others=sum(o for oi,v2,o2,e2,s2,sco2,p2 in info if p2 is not ps for o in [sco2] if o!=info[idx][4]), start=None)
        # clearer: compute per shape with unique idx
    # redo cleanly
    infos=[]
    for idx,(v,pts) in enumerate(shapes):
